newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo giro money mkt volume up on higher liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Yugo giro money mkt volume up on higher liquidity.

text.p: Turnover on Yugoslavia's unofficial market in giro money soared over the week ending August 23 at 46.350 million dinars ($9.4 million) from 40.345 million a week ago, the Belgrade bourse reported on Monday.

Traders said higher market liquidity drove the giro money market, which trades surplus liquidity among banks, and that the higher supply of free funds pushed daily interest rates slightly below 0.4 percent a day (331 percent a year).
Last week marked a return of balance between the official and unofficial financial markets, with the Belgrade bourse's weekly turnover surging to 44.064 million dinars.
According to market analysts, the balance resulted from the central bank's action regarding its auction on Friday of its short-term bonds.

In an attempt to make its short-term bonds more attractive, the bank reintroduced them with a 30-day maturity, halving their life and sharply raising their interest rate to 102.88 percent from 60.7 percent.
"The central bank has simply acknowledged market conditions," head of the brokerage Trziste Novca, Nikola Arandjelovic said.

"Until June, those bonds were the favourite instrument among investors who sought not only high return on their investment but also security for their capital, no matter how briefly their cash was tied up," he added.

According to Arandjelovic, shorter maturities always attract The higher interest rate on the central bank short-term bonds could signal a higher discount rate, but most analysts refrained from forecasts because only the central bank deputy governor and his vice-governor were responsible for setting the discount rate.

The central bank officially bases its discount rate on the interest rate for short-term bonds sold via the Belgrade bourse but also uses a basket that includes interest figures on the open money market, price rises, expected monetary developments, credit demand and money supply.

The 102.88-percent annual interest rate corresponds to 5.97 percent per month. The discount rate has been kept at 4.5 percent per month since June. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
